taylor_support: FYI support intake — multiple customers reporting 502/504 spikes from hosted inference in us-west-2a/2b since ~11:23 PST. High client-side retries and auth failures reported. I attached a trimmed log below.
ashish_net: I'm seeing packet loss and TCP retransmits on the us-west-2a <-> provider-X link. BGP flaps around 11:20-11:28. Suspect upstream provider route instability.
maria_ops: Can you paste the `mtr` or `tcptrace`? Also want to confirm whether our gateway nodes are healthy (CPU/mem/kern).
ashish_net: Here's a quick `mtr` from a gateway host to 198.51.100.23 (customer egress) taken at 11:26:
```
Start: Tue Mar 17 11:26:03 2026
HOST: gateway-usw2a        Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
 1.|-- 10.0.1.1              0.0%    20    0.2   0.3   0.1   1.4   0.3
 2.|-- 203.0.113.1           5.0%    20   20.1  21.3  19.6  50.2   7.2
 3.|-- 198.51.100.1         11.0%    20   28.2  32.8  25.4 120.6  22.7
 4.|-- 198.51.100.23        12.0%    20   35.5  40.7  33.0 130.2  25.8
```
Loss spikes at hop 2-4, aligns with provider handoff.
kevin_sre: Deploy-bot shows an automated failover to us-west-2c at 11:29 for a subset of traffic. That should reduce surface area. `deploy-bot`?
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Auto-routing: policy `edge-failover-usw2` triggered at 2026-03-17T11:29:05Z. 18% of routed inference requests shifted to us-west-2c. Monitoring for error reduction.
cassie_cs: Customer A reported 60% error rate on their /v1/generate calls, same window. They asked for ETA. What do we tell them?
maria_ops: Short term: recommend CS advise customers to retry with exponential backoff and provide a region fallback (us-west-2c or us-east-1). We're working with provider-X for mitigation.
ashish_net: Mitigation steps we executed:
- Applied BGP community to prefer transit-Y (less loaded) at 11:33.
- Temporarily blackholed a flaky nexthop for gateway-usw2a at 11:35 to avoid packet duplication.
kevin_sre: After the community change, packet loss dropped to <1% and 5xxs dropped to baseline by ~11:47. Logs:
```
Before 11:30: 5xx_rate = 4.8% (p95 latency spike)
After 11:47: 5xx_rate = 0.4%
```
ashish_net: Provider confirmed a partial interface flapping on their aggregation router. They said a patch was pushed and routes stabilized. We requested postmortem.
cassie_cs: OK sharing interim note with Customer A: "We observed an upstream provider network instability affecting a subset of us-west-2 edge nodes between 11:20-11:45 PST. We routed traffic away and worked with the provider; errors have largely subsided. We'll follow up with the final incident report and RFC." Anything else to include?
taylor_support: Add: "If you're still seeing errors, please include request IDs and timestamps; we can correlate with gateway logs and either route you to a stable region or open a priority ticket." Also offer a temporary quota bump if they hit retries that exceed limits.
kevin_sre: Action items:
- ashish_net: collect pcap for 11:20-11:40 from gateway-usw2a and upload to sec-share (sensitive -> SRE-only). due EOD.
- maria_ops: draft customer-facing interim note and post in #incidents. due +30m.
- kevin_sre: schedule postmortem with provider-X and add to incident board. due +24h.
maria_ops: Drafted interim note and posted in #incidents, pinged cs for customer templates. cc @cassie_cs
ashish_net: Uploaded sanitized pcap to sec-share at 11:58, link: https://secure-sharing.example/pcap/uw2a-8391023456.pcap
cassie_cs: Thanks — passing to Customer A. Marking urgent flag cleared for now but keeping on watch.
kevin_sre: Closing loop: 5xxs returned to normal and provider committed to a change window for long-term fix. We'll keep the incident open until provider PM gives RCA.
maria_ops: Incident status: monitoring. Will update postmortem link when available. :white_check_mark:
